unit.title: Press relations and crisis communication
unit.description: Earned media, press release, press kit, embargo, pitching journalists, spokesperson, holding statement, crisis response, right of reply

cards.definition: Paid media is bought (ads), owned media belongs to you (site, newsletter, social accounts), earned media is gained (press articles, reviews, word of mouth). PR works on earned media, which carries more trust.
cards.example: An article in Les Echos about your funding round is earned media.

cards.definition: A short news text for journalists: a factual headline, the key facts in the first paragraph (who, what, when, where, why), a quote, proof and contact details. One news item per release.
cards.example: Headline: Lyon start-up raises 5 million euros to cut food waste in canteens.

cards.definition: An agreement that journalists receive the news early but publish only after a set date and time, to prepare their articles.
cards.example: Under embargo until Tuesday 8 am: results of our study on remote work.

cards.definition: A short personal email to a journalist who covers the topic, with the angle, why it matters to their readers now, and what you can offer (data, interview, exclusive).
cards.example: A data journalist gets the study figures as an exclusive two days before the release.

cards.definition: A short first public statement in a crisis, ready in under an hour: we know, we take it seriously, here is what we are doing, next update at a given time. It buys time without lying or guessing.
cards.example: We are aware of the outage affecting payments and are working to restore it. Next update at 3 pm.

cards.definition: Speak fast, tell the truth, show empathy for people affected, act before you talk about yourself, use one spokesperson and one message, and update regularly. Silence lets others write the story.
cards.example: A food recall announced by the company itself, with clear instructions and refunds, limits the damage.

cards.definition: Under the French press law of 1881, a person or company named in a publication can demand that a reply be published in the same medium.
cards.example: A company accused in an article sends its reply to the newspaper, which must print it under the legal conditions.

exercises.prompt: A positive review of your product in a national newspaper is which kind of media?
choices: Earned
Paid
Owned
Programmatic
exercises.explain: Earned media is gained, not bought. It is why PR carries more credibility than ads.

exercises.prompt: What goes in the first paragraph of a press release?
choices: The key facts: who, what, when, where, why
The history of the company since its founding
A long quote from the CEO
The list of all the products
exercises.explain: Journalists read the top and decide. Inverted pyramid: the news first, details after.

exercises.prompt: Which press release headline is best?
choices: Lyon start-up raises 5 million euros to cut canteen food waste
A great new step in our wonderful history
Innovation and passion at the heart of our project
We are proud to share some exciting news
exercises.explain: Factual, specific, newsworthy. Adjectives and pride do not make news.

exercises.prompt: What does under embargo until Tuesday 8 am mean?
choices: Journalists can prepare the story but publish only from Tuesday 8 am
The news is cancelled after Tuesday morning
Only media that pay may publish the story
The release must stay secret forever
exercises.explain: Embargoes let media prepare quality coverage. Breaking one damages the relationship.

exercises.prompt: How do you pitch a journalist?
choices: A short personal email with an angle for their readers
The same release sent to 2,000 addresses
Several calls a day until they answer
A gift with no news attached
exercises.explain: Target the right person, explain why it matters now for their audience, offer something useful.

exercises.prompt: A bug leaks customer emails. When should the first statement come out?
choices: Within the hour, as a holding statement
After the full investigation, weeks later
Never, to avoid drawing attention
Only if a journalist calls
exercises.explain: A fast, honest holding statement keeps control of the story. Data breaches also have legal duties: the CNIL within 72 hours, and sometimes the people affected.

exercises.prompt: In a crisis, several managers giving different answers to the press shows transparency.
exercises.explain: False. One spokesperson and one message avoid contradictions that turn into a second story.

exercises.prompt: What should a holding statement do?
choices: Acknowledge, show concern, say what is done, set the next update
Explain in detail which employee is to blame
Deny everything until it is proven otherwise
Promote a big discount to change the subject
exercises.explain: It buys time without lying or guessing, and sets when you will speak again.

exercises.prompt: A newspaper names your company in an inaccurate article. What French legal tool exists?
choices: The right of reply under the 1881 press law
Asking the CNIL to delete the article
A cookie banner complaint
Nothing, the press is free
exercises.explain: The right of reply lets a named person or company have an answer published in the same medium.

exercises.prompt: Put a crisis response in order.
steps: Check the facts and assess the impact quickly
Act to protect the people affected
Give regular updates through one spokesperson
Review what happened and fix the cause
exercises.explain: Facts, first word, action, regular updates, then learning. Acting matters more than talking.
